title: The 3 Best Dog Crates for Apartments
h1: The 3 Best Dog Crates for Apartments
metaDescription: Our 3 picks for dog crates for apartments, with key specs, strengths and limitations for each, based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports.
lede: We looked at dog crates for apartments using manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. Each pick lists what it does well and where it falls short, so you can match it to how you'll use it.

products.name: MidWest iCrate 36-Inch Double Door Dog Crate
products.blurb: Key specs: Folds flat for storage, 36"L x 23"W x 25"H, Rubber feet reduce floor noise and scratching.
strengths: Folds down to a few inches thick, easy to tuck away when not set up
Rubber feet protect rental flooring and cut down on rattling
Mid-size footprint works in most one-bedroom and studio layouts
limitations: Still a real footprint once set up, measure your space before buying
Wire sides offer no visual privacy without an added cover
No wheels for repositioning within the apartment
features: Rubber feet reduce floor noise and scratching

products.name: SportPet Designs Sport Pet Large Portable Kennel
products.blurb: Key specs: Lightweight folding wire construction, Carrying handle, Quick fold and setup.
strengths: Easiest crate in this list to carry between rooms or to a car
Lightweight build is ideal for apartment dwellers who move often
Quick fold makes it practical for weekend trips as well as home use
limitations: Lighter wire gauge than the iCrate, best for calm dogs
Fewer size options than MidWest's lineup
Not rated for dogs that chew or lean hard on the frame

products.name: MidWest LifeStages 24-Inch Double Door Dog Crate
strengths: Folds flat with a carry handle
limitations: Some dogs learn to push the pan

howWeChose: Picks are based on manufacturer specs, independent reviews and owner reports. We don't claim our own testing.
We do not list prices or star ratings because they change. Check Amazon for current details.
